fieldMarks: 5-8.5 in (12.5-21.5 cm); gray, brown or black with five white or yellowish stripes (two per side, one down the back).
Young have a bright blue tail; adult male stripes may fade and a reddish or orange colour may develop on the head.
No enlarged row of scales under the tail, unlike five-lined and broadhead skinks.
behavior: Found on the ground or in trees, but less arboreal than broadhead skinks; most often beneath logs or under bark and runs for the nearest tree or log when pursued.
Eats a wide variety of insects, spiders and other invertebrates.
Females lay several eggs in moist soil or rotten logs in summer and attend them; tail breaks off when restrained.
habitat: Dry wooded habitats with abundant fallen trees and stumps, especially dry pine forests and coastal areas; also wet pine flatwoods, sandhills and abandoned buildings.
range: Throughout South Carolina and all but extreme northern Georgia (SREL); the wider range was not sourced in detail. Not in Canada.

lookalikes.name: Common five-lined skink
lookalikes.howToTell: Five-lined skink has an enlarged row of scales under the tail and usually uses moister habitat.

lookalikes.name: Broadhead skink
lookalikes.howToTell: Broadhead skinks are usually larger and more arboreal, and have an enlarged row of scales under the tail.
